name: Bell 427
summary: A light twin-turbine Bell with a four-blade rotor and smooth lines, a twin-engine cousin of the 407.

wings: Four-blade bearingless main rotor on a smooth mast
Mast fairing blending into the cowling
engines: Twin turboshafts under the rear roof
Two exhausts at the rear of the engine deck
fuselage: Smooth swept cabin with large windows
tail: Slim boom with a swept fin and horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Four-blade rotor on a smooth swept light twin
Two exhausts at the rear of the engine deck

confusedWith.howToTell: The 407 has one engine and a single exhaust; the 427 is slightly longer with twin exhausts.
The 429 is noticeably larger, with a bigger rear cabin; the 427 is smaller.
The 206 has a two-blade rotor and a rounder body; the 427 has four blades and a smoother, swept body.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
